newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia to buy $46 mln of oil from neighbours.
newsitem.headline: Zambia to buy $46 mln of oil from neighbours.

text.p: Zambia is to import fuel worth $46 million from her neighbours to cover a 45-day shortfall resulting from repair work at Dar-es-Salaam port in Tanzania, Energy Minister Edith Nawakwi said on Friday.
She told parliament that a consignment of petroleum feedstock had been held up at the port for nearly two months because of the work.
"The date of completion of these works...has been a moving target, resulting in the feedstock lying idle in the harbour for about 50 days," she said.
"It is against this background that imports of 45 stock days are required to sustain the normal supply to consumers."
Zambia would import 22,500 cubic metres of petrol, 42,000 cubic metres of diesel, 13,500 cubic metres of kerosene and 10,500 cubic metres of fuel oil.
"The total cost of importing these quantities is estimated at 60 billion kwacha ($46 million)," Nawakwi said.
She said state-run Zambia National Oil Company had already started importing petroleum products from Zimbabwe, Tanzania and Namibia using road tankers.
The company would import 22 days' supply of petrol and 11 days of diesel.
